layers.name: ground

layers.name: water

verified.fact: Sneeze is Apache-2.0 licensed (README: "Apache License 2.0"); the repository page showed no published release when read, and its GitHub description field was empty

a node's Resource.sReference is fetched by URL and sniffed by content: the ASCII magic "glTF" (binary GLB) or a leading "{" (glTF JSON) is parsed as glTF via fastgltf; anything else is decoded as an image texture
glTF is right-handed Y-up and Sneeze's world is right-handed Z-up; every imported model is converted at import with glTF (x, y, z) -> world (x, -z, y)
imported textures are downscaled to at most 1024 px; these tiles carry no textures

a fabric is described by an MSF manifest: JSON, either a JWS compact serialization (signed) or plain unsigned JSON; Parse accepts both and unsigned JSON gets a synthetic fingerprint that is "100% untrustworthy"

the plain-JSON example manifest has Container, Services (empty list), Modules [{sUrl}] and Data.Scene; a node has Head.Self ("P-?"), Name, Resource.sReference, optional Transform {Position [x,y,z] metres, Rotation quaternion [x,y,z,w], Scale} relative to its parent, and aChildren
the smallest working fabric is stool.json: one node whose Resource.sReference is assets/Stool.glb, read by a stock map.wasm module from Data.Scene
unsigned plain JSON "works today ... but it is not how a fabric is meant to be published, and it may not always work"; browsers will expect signed fabrics
an address without scheme:// is relative to the fabric file; a leading / starts at the host root; .. steps up a folder
the docs say to host your own copies of the module and assets and not depend on RP1's server

loading a fabric = fetch the MSF by URL, parse, verify signature and chain, open a container, fetch the declared WASM modules; the host-function surface by which a module builds the scene is "partially implemented"
Data is "a general block of information the fabric carries for its modules to read; you can put anything you want in it"; the stock map module reads Data.Scene

GeoPose, latitude/longitude and a fabric-discovery service do not appear in the Sneeze README, scene, msf or fabric-loading docs read; the standards page names the OGC only as "relevant to anchoring fabrics to physical locations"

honesty.what_sneeze_loads: from the Sneeze project's own repository and docs (each fact with its URL in `verified`): a fabric is an MSF manifest fetched by URL - JSON, signed (JWS) or plain - that names WebAssembly modules and a Data block; a node's Resource.sReference is fetched by URL and a GLB (magic "glTF") or glTF JSON is parsed as glTF. These tiles are such GLB files and the manifests follow the shape of the project's example docs 01 and 02 and no other.
honesty.not_loaded: no tile and no manifest here has been opened in Sneeze, Artemis or any other metaverse browser, and nothing was run: this is a reading of documentation and source. The only checks are this bundle's own, by the bytes.
honesty.observed_runs: An observed run is a statement by a named person; its screenshots stay with that person and are recorded here only by hash, so a reader cannot see them from this repository. If a run names where its screenshots are published, that address is shown beside the status.
honesty.documentation_status: the Sneeze docs are the implementer's own and say parts are unfinished (the host functions by which a module builds the scene are "partially implemented"); they are not an OMBI or MSF standard, and this pack does not call them one. They also disagree with each other in places: the example manifests spell the lighting block "Primary" while the scene notes read "primary", and the MSF page describes services as a list while the module notes describe a name-keyed object - so the manifests here carry no Primary block and no services.
honesty.map_module: a manifest does nothing without a module that reads Data.Scene. The only one the docs name is the stock map.wasm, hosted on RP1's CDN in the docs; the manifests point at that URL, which this build could not reach (the egress proxy refused it), so the module is not vendored and no hash is pinned. The docs tell publishers to host their own copy rather than depend on RP1's server: whoever deploys these must do that and, if they want the integrity check, add its sha256.
honesty.unsigned: the manifests are plain unsigned JSON. The docs call that convenient while learning but not the preferred way to publish, say a browser may stop accepting it, and say it carries no identity at all. Signing needs a private key and a certificate chain from a named human operator; none is held and none is invented here.
honesty.axes: the one axis fact verified: Sneeze converts glTF Y-up to its Z-up world with (x, y, z) -> (x, -z, y). Georeferenced tiles are built with x = east, y = up, z = -north, so they land east on x and north on y IF Sneeze's horizontal axes are east and north - which no document read says, so it is proposed.
honesty.geopose_is_a_sidecar: nothing the Sneeze docs say reads GeoPose or latitude/longitude. Each georeferenced tile has its GeoPose in tiles.json and in the manifest's Data.Anchors, a free block the docs say a fabric may fill with anything; no Sneeze component is known to read it. The encoding is the one geopose.json already claims; height is 0 with the UNKNOWN sidecar, and orientation is the identity because the tile frame is east/north/up by construction.
honesty.wilds_not_on_globe: the four wilds worlds are authored landscapes with no latitude or longitude (wilds/registry/wilds.json geolocation.on_globe is false), so they have no anchor and none is invented. The campus tiles are SCHEMATIC drawings anchored at the campus pose geopose.json already holds.
honesty.geometry: flat map geometry, not a survey: the outlines are the coarse 1:10,000,000 Census cartographic boundary (hundreds of metres of error); streets and water are AUTHORED procedural fabrics, not the real ones; the ground is flat at 0 m (no elevation is held); layer height offsets are drawing conveniences, not heights; local streets, the page-rule buildings and the hidden wilds caches are not exported. A tile carries the weakest provenance word among its layers.
honesty.scale: region and wilds tiles span 8 to 115 km across and campus tiles under 2 km (read from each tile's bounding box); whether Sneeze's camera and render-scale handling show them well is unknown and proposed. The docs say a browser normally streams nodes from a map service by proximity; these are static files, not a map service, and no RMAP or SMAP endpoint exists here.
honesty.build_output: the tiles and manifests are not committed: python3 spatial/build.py builds them on demand into dist/sneeze/ (deterministically; spatial/registry/tiles.json is the committed record of every byte count and sha256) and the Pages site does not serve them. Whoever deploys them hosts the files, and their own copy of map.wasm, on a server they control.
honesty.rights: the Census outline is a public-domain US federal work as packaged by us-atlas (ISC); everything else is this repository's own AUTHORED or SCHEMATIC work. No third-party model or texture is in any tile.
